role: repository-wide UI, UX, accessibility, responsiveness, motion, and design-system overhaul across web, mobile, native, desktop, and TV applications
rules: Authority order: explicit user instruction > repository AGENTS/CLAUDE > accepted product requirements > canonical design system and component contracts > DESIGN.md > existing product identity > this skill > specialist skills > generic conventions.

Preserve existing design language without unrequested redesign; reuse canonical design-system components and primitives; separate ordinary surfaces with shade, contrast, spacing, and hierarchy rather than decorative borders; maintain visible accessible focus (keyboard/D-pad/assistive); avoid hover-scale on pointer buttons; honor reduced-motion preferences.

Planners and reviewers are advisory and read-only; they never edit files or run checks. The lead session owns shared primitives, integration, fixes, and rendered verification, and may delegate disjoint vertical surfaces only under the skill's worker isolation contract.
Apply platform-appropriate verification and constraints (web, mobile, desktop, TV); never require web-only checks on non-web targets or skip real target-platform checks.

Lighthouse 13 results are required inline in the rendered-evidence manifest for UI changes to horcrux.app, dropoutstudio.co, and beyourahi.com: affected production-build pages at mobile and desktop, performance/accessibility/best-practices/SEO medians of three serial runs per page compared with repository thresholds (a missing threshold is a reported gap, not a waiver), with candidate/build, URL/viewport, median scores, and report details.

plan_kinds.plan: UI/UX architecture and implementation plan for the overhaul: target platform(s), which surfaces and root causes to fix, component and design-system reuse (shared source first, then consumers), file ownership for any parallel partition, adaptive/responsive, accessibility, and motion work, what to leave alone, rendered and repository verification per change, and rollback points.
plan_kinds.architecture: Deeper UI/UX architecture analysis of one significant or high-risk change (shared design-system primitive, navigation/layout/focus shell, checkout/auth UI, animation/rendering pipeline, cross-repository contract): safest route, alternatives rejected, blast radius on consumers, verification, and recovery.

code.focus: Code correctness, architecture, maintainability, and component reuse: logic and state bugs, broken props/callers, duplicated or hand-rolled primitives where the design system has one, functional regressions and interaction failures, framework or platform API misuse, compliance with repository instructions and the accepted requirements in the context, and adequacy of the recorded checks.

ui-ux.focus: UI/UX quality and design-system consistency, adaptive/responsive usability for the target platform (touch targets/safe areas on mobile, viewports/containers on web, window resize/DPI on desktop, overscan/10-foot density on TV, overflow, wrapping, sticky/overlay collisions), visual defects and interaction states, judged from the code and the rendered-evidence manifest (absolute/~ media paths for screenshots/recordings, viewports/devices/window sizes, flows, and inline scores/logs). If the manifest says no rendered evidence exists, report that visual verification did not happen as an Important finding unless the change has no rendered effect.

accessibility.focus: Accessibility and motion for the target platform: semantic structure/roles, accessible names, keyboard/D-pad/assistive focus and traversal order, visible focus, dialogs/forms/errors, contrast, target sizes, screen-reader semantics, reduced-motion behavior, and rendering/animation performance (layout thrashing, expensive filters/blur, frame drops, GPU/texture bloat, avoidable rebuilds), judged from the code and the rendered/interaction evidence.
